quiz.q: Why did Kaja Kallas push back so firmly when Trump said a deal with Moscow 'might involve all of Europe'?
options: The EU wants to replace NATO with its own army
A deal on Europe's security reached without Europeans would let Russia shape arrangements EU states must then live with and enforce
EU law forbids any talks with Russia
The EU had already signed its own peace treaty with Russia
quiz.explain: [[p:Kaja Kallas]] argued that Europe already has a security architecture and that Moscow has no veto over it. EU states would have to implement much of any settlement, from sanctions to security guarantees, so they want a seat rather than a briefing afterwards.

quiz.q: What makes the Student List's win in Serbia different from most opposition victories?
options: It won by joining Vučić's coalition
It grew out of a protest movement rather than an established party and won an outright majority alone
It won only because turnout collapsed
It was elected by parliament, not by voters
quiz.explain: The [[p:Student List]] came out of the protest movement and took 140 of 250 seats on the highest turnout in over 30 years, so it can govern without coalition bargaining, ending [[p:Aleksandar Vučić]]'s long dominance.

quiz.q: Why can Hungary still slow Ukraine's EU talks even after lifting its earlier veto?
options: Hungary holds the EU presidency
Every step, including approving screening reports and opening each cluster, needs unanimous agreement
Hungary controls the European Commission's enlargement department
Ukraine's candidate status expired
quiz.explain: Accession runs on unanimity at each stage. Budapest let clusters 2 and 3 open but has not approved the screening reports for clusters 4 and 5, so one government can delay progress step by step.

quiz.q: France's National Assembly rejected the 2027 budget. What does that mean for the government?
options: France immediately runs out of money
The budget goes to the Senate unamended, and the government may later force it through with Article 49.3, ordinances or a stopgap law
President Macron must resign
The EU takes over France's budget
quiz.explain: Rejecting the revenue part kills the bill at first reading but not the process. [[p:Sébastien Lecornu]] has no majority, so he must either strike a non-censure deal or use tools that bypass a vote, each risking a censure motion.

quiz.q: Why does the US 'Task Force Iron Gate' matter for the US–Iran confrontation?
options: It ends the naval blockade
It extends pressure from the sea to Iran's land borders and the Caspian, routes the blockade does not cover
It is a joint US–Iranian peacekeeping force
It replaces Qatari mediation
quiz.explain: The naval blockade targets Gulf shipping, but Iran can still trade overland and across the Caspian. The task force aims at those routes, even as Qatar mediates and the [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] answers by lifting its 2,000 km missile-range cap.
